perspective:
Carolyn Abebe’s accessible perspective/information:

- She knows Marilyn as a colleague at the community bank and has recently started working with her.
- During a busy/stressful week, Carolyn observed Marilyn being unusually quiet and withdrawn for several days, unlike her normally engaging demeanor.
- Carolyn asked Marilyn if everything was alright and whether she wanted to talk. Marilyn told her she was overwhelmed by work and some personal stuff, and thanked her for asking.
- In a later interaction, Carolyn experienced Marilyn responding curtly and felt confused and slightly hurt.
- Carolyn told Marilyn she hoped she hadn’t overstepped, and shared that she had had tough times too and that talking sometimes helped. Marilyn replied that she appreciated it, apologized if she seemed off, and said it had been a hard week.
- Carolyn perceived Marilyn as responding positively to her openness and felt relieved and hopeful about their friendship.
- Carolyn invited Marilyn to a small weekend get-together with friends. Marilyn accepted, saying it sounded lovely and thanking her.
- Carolyn perceived that, despite friendly interactions outside work, Marilyn still kept a professional distance at the bank. This made Carolyn feel disappointed.
- Carolyn asked Marilyn to talk about their work dynamic, saying she felt a distance she couldn’t understand. Marilyn said she hadn’t realized it, apologized if it seemed that way, and agreed to talk about improving collaboration.
- After their private meeting/talk, Carolyn believed they had cleared the air and better understood each other’s professional expectations and personal boundaries; she felt content and optimistic.
- Carolyn proposed teaming up on the new project proposal. Marilyn agreed, said she was glad they had talked, and said she looked forward to working more closely with her.

Carolyn does not have specific details about Marilyn’s personal situation beyond “work and personal stuff” and “a hard week,” nor confirmed access to Marilyn’s private inner feelings beyond what Marilyn said and Carolyn observed.
